material.text_fr: Dans le tiroir d'Odile, un Polaroid : un port, des bateaux, et « 1971 » au dos.
Vous avez promis à M. Marchand de retrouver le peintre « L. » avant son anniversaire.
Aider Margaux à refaire la carte du Mistral avant le printemps.
L'avenir du Mistral : le garder, le changer, ou le laisser partir ?
Gus a reçu une lettre d'un notaire, avec un timbre étranger, et il ne l'ouvre pas.
Romy vous a demandé d'être la voix française de son documentaire radio.
Lila et Berlin : peut-on vouloir quelqu'un ici, et vouloir son départ pour elle ?
Qui était Odile, et pourquoi est-elle partie ?
Rue de Lancry, au troisième, une fenêtre est encore allumée.

departed.name: Lila Bonnet
departed.why: Lila left for Berlin on 8 January (T8, the platform) and lives there now.

rules: The whole cast knows the learner: never a stranger's welcome, never the vous of strangers from the group.
The continuation may look for «L.», ask about the rue de Lancry, follow the painting; it never reveals who L. is — that answer belongs to the next authored season.
facts: The learner kept Odile's flat above Le Mistral and lives there now.
Le Mistral is exactly as it was; Margaux runs it alone, on a nine-year lease.
M. Marchand left the building for a residence without stairs; Solvel owns his floors, he kept the café's walls.
Only four people know Odile's notebook page; Gus knows nothing of it.
The painting «Le Mistral sur le canal» is with the learner; its back reads «Pour Odile, qui part. — L., 1970» and «Toujours rue de Lancry. — L., 2021».
Marin has put his co-op folder in a drawer.
Lila left for Berlin on 8 January; she lives there now. She writes; she is never in a Paris scene.
Odile's last letter has been read: she left two things in Paris, the flat and someone; for the other, «regarde derrière le tableau du Mistral».
Camille Marchand has met the learner and still says vous; the switch to tu belongs to a later season.
The café question of season 1 is closed. Do not reopen it.
M. Marchand comes to Sunday lunch at the learner's, by the 46 bus, as he did at Odile's.
Romy gave the learner the memory card with Margaux's admission, without a word.

draft.logline: After a Polaroid and a promise, the learner follows a trail from Paris to Papeete: they enter a Tahitian cooking competition to meet locals, help Romy record a radio documentary, and chase clues about the painter L. and Gus's mysterious foreign letter — all while deciding what Odile's life means to them.
draft.logline_fr: Vous partez à Papeete pour chercher L. et participer à un concours de cuisine.
draft.your_arc: You go because you promised to find the painter L.; the season is about turning a private promise into a public, messy search: you learn to ask strangers, to hold a friend's secrets, and to come home with a different sense of what 'keeping' someone means.
draft.first_episode_seed: You find the Polaroid of a sunlit port in Odile's drawer (1971) and remember your promise to M. Marchand to find the painter 'L.' Romy recognizes the harbour as Tahiti; at the same time Gus receives a letter with a foreign stamp. You decide to fly: Romy as recorder and Gus (reluctant) come with you; a local chef invites you to the island cooking contest that will open doors.

stages.summary: A Polaroid (1971) and the promise to M. Marchand send you to Papeete to look for the painter L.; Mana invites you into the competition as an access point.
At the market and harbour the memories fragment: people remember an artist, but names shift and the trail cools.
A pensioner at the guesthouse recalls a nickname and points to a boat log — you gain a new clue that keeps the search alive without revealing L.'s identity.
Gus's unopened letter arrives with a foreign stamp and a postmark that points to French Polynesia, giving him a reason to come with you.
A small gallery owner (Hikaru) reads the name on the letter and finds only a traveler's reference number and a 1971 date — the lead seems archival and hard to follow.
Gus decides to open the letter in Papeete; it contains a postcard and a penciled line that points to a boat and a date, but not a name — Gus keeps part of the revelation to himself.
Romy asks you to be the French voice of her radio documentary; recording in market kitchens brings private memories about Odile into the open.
Romy hears a recording that could change how friends see Odile; she hesitates to broadcast something that would hurt people back in Paris.
Romy crafts a piece that honors Odile's wandering life without naming private betrayals; the documentary gives you a public image of Odile that helps you feel less alone.
The Polaroid and seaside conversations make you wonder who Odile was beyond Paris and whether her life included leaving for good.
Being far from the flat and in a bright new place, you feel the pull of adventure and the pull of the home you already kept.
You return to Paris with a new picture of Odile's life — not answers to everything, but a feeling that keeping the flat was the right choice for now.

open_threads.text: Find the painter called 'L.' before M. Marchand's birthday; local nicknames, boat logs, and gallery notes may point the way.
open_threads.text_fr: Je dois trouver le peintre L. avant l'anniversaire de M. Marchand.

open_threads.text: Open and decipher Gus's foreign-stamped letter: it contains a postcard and a coded note with a 1971 date.
open_threads.text_fr: La lettre de Gus a un timbre étranger; je dois l'ouvrir.

open_threads.text: Record Romy's documentary material in Tahiti without exposing friends back in Paris; choose what to say on air.
open_threads.text_fr: Je suis la voix française du documentaire de Romy.

open_threads.text: Who was Odile, and where did she go when she left Paris? The Polaroid and island stories give pieces but no final name.
open_threads.text_fr: Qui était Odile et où elle est partie ?

setting.neighborhood: the harbour, market and guesthouses near the foreshore
setting.tone: sunny, tense, curious — reality-competition energy with intimate questions
setting.situation: You travel to Papeete to follow clues about the painter L., to keep your promise to M. Marchand, and you enter a local cooking competition to meet people who knew Odile.
setting.situation_fr: Vous allez à Papeete pour chercher L. et participer à un concours de cuisine.
setting.why: The material promise to M. Marchand (b:peintre_l) and a Polaroid of a port (p:polaroid_port) point to an overseas harbour; the promise forces you to go before his birthday and the Polaroid + Gus's foreign-stamped letter make Tahiti the plausible lead.

places.description: A busy open-air market by the harbour where fishermen, produce sellers and artisans meet; characters ask questions, trade memories, and find small paper clues or old photos.
places.brief: Rows of wooden stalls under woven sunshades; piles of papaya and taro, hanging fish, a string of coloured flags; warm early-morning light and wet, glinting stone floors.

places.description: The port where the Polaroid seems to have been taken — small boats, freight activity and a sleepy quay that holds local gossip and older travellers who might have known Odile or L.
places.brief: A corrugated pier with moored pirogues, a concrete quay stained by salt, ropes and a faded sign with peeling paint; strong mid-morning sun and reflective water.

places.description: A pop-up competition kitchen turned arena (open to the public) where contestants cook Tahitian dishes on camera; a place to meet food people who tell stories and to record Romy's sound bites.
places.brief: A long stainless-steel counter under studio lights, plastic crates of fruit at the back, a scoreboard on the wall, late-afternoon golden light through high windows.

places.description: A modest guesthouse on a side street where old students, sailors and ex-pat artists sometimes live; it gives a private nook where an elderly witness can recall a nickname without naming L.
places.brief: A narrow white house with a wooden veranda, a hammock tied to two posts, jars of dried fish on a shelf, dusk cooling the painted shutters.

places.description: An atoll a short boat ride away — quiet, with an older painter's colony vibe; a place for a decisive, sunlit conversation that reframes Odile's past without revealing L.'s identity.
places.brief: Shallow turquoise lagoon, a leaning coconut palm, a small reef visible in transparent water; late-afternoon sun at slant, soft sand.

new_characters.name: Mana Teiva
new_characters.role: Local chef and producer of the island's popular cooking contest; she invites the learner to compete as a way to meet island storytellers.
new_characters.personality: Direct, warm, loves to teach; likes people who cook with memory.
new_characters.wants: To showcase Tahitian cooks and to discover the island stories behind recipes.
new_characters.speech_pattern: Clear French with Tahitian turns of phrase; she speaks firmly and punctuates sentences with small local words.

new_characters.name: Hikaru Tavita
new_characters.role: Small gallery owner and restorer who occasionally handles older travel photographs and paintings and who recognizes the style on the back of the Mistral painting.
new_characters.personality: Careful, slightly theatrical, loves provenance stories; he follows paper trails.
new_characters.wants: To document the island's artistic exchanges and to make a small catalogue of visiting painters.
new_characters.speech_pattern: Measured French with a habit of naming colours and dates; precise and knowingly playful.

new_characters.name: Tiare Manoa
new_characters.role: Fisher and small-time seller of old photos and postcards at the market; remembers an artist who painted boats and who sometimes traded paintings for meals.
new_characters.personality: Practical, affectionate, speaks in anecdotes; loves to barter stories as much as goods.
new_characters.wants: To keep a small memory economy alive — photos, recipes, and names.
new_characters.speech_pattern: Informal French with island rhythm; quick, economical sentences.

issues: Do not reveal the identity of « L. ». The canon explicitly reserves that answer for the next authored season; the proposal correctly promises not to reveal it, but this must be enforced in all payoff scenes.

Careful with Gus's new knowledge: canon says Gus knows nothing of Odile's notebook page. The season may show Gus learning archival facts or receiving a letter (p:lettre_gus) but must not retroactively make him aware of the notebook or its contents.

The Café question from season 1 is closed. The proposal keeps Le Mistral and the flat and does not reopen the save/change/leave debate — maintain that closure in all Paris scenes (no new sale-threat or co‑op arc).

Genre and location jump (Paris → Papeete, culinary competition) are strong and welcome for freshness, but they reduce time in the established Paris locations and with the familiar slice-of-life tone. Ensure the learner still has regular, explicit linguistic and social returns to Le Mistral / the apartment so A2 learners keep anchor vocabulary and recurring characters.

Register and dialect: island characters have Tahitian turns and different registers (tu/vous). The materials must scaffold these differences for A2 learners (glosses, repetition, simpler intermediary lines) so that comprehension stays learner-facing.

Practical timing: the promise to find L. before M. Marchand's birthday must remain a believable deadline in-story (travel time, logistics). The season should show the learner's motivation pulled from the material (b:peintre_l and p:polaroid_port) clearly in early episodes so the move to Tahiti feels demanded, not optional.

Romy's moral dilemma about what to broadcast (b:documentaire) is well-grounded but sensitive: avoid a forced public betrayal of friends. Keep Romy's reluctance and editorial care consistent with canon ('she does not want to publish the thing that breaks her friends').
Keep Lila absent from Paris scenes (canon: Lila left for Berlin and is never in Paris scenes). The proposal does not reintroduce her physically — maintain that constraint.
